lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Okay, before we design anything else, let's be honest with each other about money.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Agreed. I pulled the numbers last night and it's tighter than I was telling people.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How tight?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: We have four thousand dollars for the whole first version. That's the entire budget. Design, build, hosting, all of it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Four thousand. Okay. That's not nothing, but it isn't much either.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's what's left after the hardware. And there's nothing more coming until we can show somebody a working thing.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So every decision from here has to fit inside four thousand dollars. Let's just say that out loud and mean it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's how I'd frame it, yeah.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Alright. What actually eats money? My guess is the recognition model.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Maybe eventually. But we could start with an off the shelf vision API and pay per call.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Which at our volume is basically free, because our volume is basically zero.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Ten users costs us pennies. Honestly, the API isn't the problem this year.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good. So where does it actually hurt?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The look of it, I think. It has to feel trustworthy, or nobody is going to photograph the inside of their fridge.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's fair. A sloppy interface reads as, this thing is probably going to get it wrong.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And we are both engineers, so.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So neither of us is going to make it beautiful. Yeah, I've accepted that.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So what do you want to do about it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Here's my actual idea. There's that design studio my old coworker used. They'd do the whole thing, brand, every screen, a proper design system.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And how much are we talking for that?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Twenty thousand, roughly. Maybe twenty-two with the brand work. I think we should just book them for the first version.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And we'd get the full set of screens out of that, not just a logo?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The full set, plus a style guide we keep building against for years.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That is a real option. I'd want to see their last two projects.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'd rather spend once and have it right than redo it three times badly.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Let's sit with it for a day and pick it up tomorrow.

moments.description: B sets the entire first-version budget at four thousand dollars (line 3) and A agrees every decision has to fit inside it (line 6). At line 20 A proposes booking a twenty thousand dollar design studio for that same first version.
